draft.title: Differential equations
card: A differential equation links a quantity to its rate of change. For example, dy/dt = 3y says the rate of change of y is 3 times y.

To form one from a context, write the rate as a derivative and set it equal to what the words describe. "A tank loses salt at a rate proportional to the amount S present" gives dS/dt = −kS, with k > 0.
A solution is a function that makes the equation true. To check one, differentiate it and substitute both y and dy/dt into the equation.
Worked check: is y = 2e^(3t) a solution of dy/dt = 3y? Differentiating gives dy/dt = 6e^(3t). Also 3y = 3 × 2e^(3t) = 6e^(3t). The two sides match, so it is a solution.
draft.remember: Write the rate as a derivative to form the equation. Substitute the function and its derivative to check a solution.

a.q: A biologist says the rate of growth of a bacteria population N is proportional to N, with constant k > 0. Which differential equation matches?
a.why: A rate of change is written as dN/dt, and proportional to N means it equals k times N. The option dN/dt = k is tempting, but that rate stays the same whatever N is, so it is not proportional to N.
a.clue: Rate means a derivative, and proportional means a constant multiple of N.

b.q: Which function is a solution of dy/dt = −2y?
b.why: For y = 5e^(−2t), dy/dt = −10e^(−2t), and −2y = −2 × 5e^(−2t) = −10e^(−2t). The two sides match. For y = 5e^(2t), dy/dt = 10e^(2t), but −2y = −10e^(2t), so the sign is wrong.
b.clue: Differentiate each function, then compare dy/dt with −2y.

problems.detail: The clue says rate means a derivative and proportional means a constant multiple of N. Together these state dN/dt = kN outright, so a student can pick the answer without forming the equation themselves.

check.summary: The card, answers and explanations are correct. The only problem is that question a's clue spells out the answer (rate is a derivative, proportional is a constant multiple of N), so it should hint without stating it.

final.title: Differential equations
card: A differential equation links a quantity to its rate of change. For example, \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 3y\) says the rate of change of \(y\) is 3 times \(y\).

To form one from a context, write the rate as a derivative and set it equal to what the words describe. "A tank loses salt at a rate proportional to the amount \(S\) present" gives \(\frac{dS}{dt} = -kS\), with \(k > 0\).
A solution is a function that makes the equation true. To check one, differentiate it and substitute both \(y\) and \(\frac{dy}{dt}\) into the equation.

Worked check: is \(y = 2e^{3t}\) a solution of \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 3y\)? Differentiating gives \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 6e^{3t}\). Also \(3y = 3 \times 2e^{3t} = 6e^{3t}\). The two sides match, so it is a solution.
final.remember: Write the rate as a derivative to form the equation. Substitute the function and its derivative to check a solution.

a.q: A biologist says the rate of growth of a bacteria population \(N\) is proportional to \(N\), with constant \(k > 0\). Which differential equation matches?
a.why: A rate of change is written as \(\frac{dN}{dt}\), and proportional to \(N\) means it equals \(k\) times \(N\). The option \(\frac{dN}{dt} = k\) is tempting, but that rate stays the same whatever \(N\) is, so it is not proportional to \(N\).
a.clue: Follow the same steps used for the salt tank on the card.

b.q: Which function is a solution of \(\frac{dy}{dt} = -2y\)?
b.why: For \(y = 5e^{-2t}\), \(\frac{dy}{dt} = -10e^{-2t}\), and \(-2y = -2 \times 5e^{-2t} = -10e^{-2t}\). The two sides match. For \(y = 5e^{2t}\), \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 10e^{2t}\), but \(-2y = -10e^{2t}\), so the sign is wrong.
b.clue: Differentiate each function, then compare \(\frac{dy}{dt}\) with \(-2y\).
